title: The Man Who Walked Off the Titanic With the Key #history #shorts
description:
Days before the Titanic sailed, Second Officer David Blair was moved off the ship, and he left with a key in his pocket. For a century it has been called the key to the lookouts' binoculars, and lookout Fred Fleet told the US inquiry that with glasses they could have seen the iceberg in time "to get out of the way."

But the brass tag on the real key reads "Crows Nest Telephone Key." Lookout George Hogg testified that Blair had him lock the binoculars in Blair's cabin at Southampton, and when the lookouts asked for glasses at sea, Lightoller told them there were none. The key sold for £90,000 in 2007. Historians still disagree about which lock it opened.
